 SKIP ADVERTISEMENT ‘I Know How Much You Love the American People,’ Trump Told Biden in 2021 Letter
 The letter, which former President Joseph R. Biden Jr. details in a new book, is remarkable for a warm tone starkly at odds with his predecessor’s public comments.
 Listen · 6:12 min Share full article 
 495 
 President Joseph R. Biden Jr. at his inauguration in 2021, which President Trump had refused to attend. Credit... Chang W. Lee/The New York Times By Tyler Pager 
 Nov. 10, 2026

 In his first week in office, President Joseph R. Biden Jr. told reporters that his immediate predecessor, Donald J. Trump, had left him a “very generous letter” in the Oval Office. Since then, Mr. Biden has refused to discuss the contents.
 But in his new book, “Promise Me, America,” Mr. Biden reprints the letter in full, according to an excerpt obtained by The New York Times. The Times also reviewed a photocopy of the original letter, which was dated Jan. 20, 2021, and left in an envelope addressed “To ‘46’” — a reference to Mr. Biden’s status as the 46th president.
 The letter, written on White House stationery with Mr. Trump’s signature black Sharpie, is remarkable for how discordant it is with Mr. Trump’s public comments about Mr. Biden and the 2020 presidential election. Mr. Trump did not criticize Mr. Biden or challenge the results of the election. Instead, he wrote almost poetically about his experience working in the White House and how he believed that Mr. Biden “will be true to yourself and the American people.”
 “Many presidents have come and gone who simply governed as Republicans or Democrats,” Mr. Trump wrote. “Largely, they did not change history, they were just swept along in its relentless tide. This will not happen to you because I know how much you love the American people.”
 In his book, which will be released next Tuesday, Mr. Biden, 83, writes that it was “as if there were two Donald Trumps.” He says Mr. Trump “deeply destabilized our democracy” and had “not offered the traditional meeting between presidents.”
 “But here he was, offering his best wishes in warm language that sounded like it was coming from an old friend,” Mr. Biden writes.
